newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Aer Lingus signs deal with Lufthansa Technik.
newsitem.headline: Aer Lingus signs deal with Lufthansa Technik.

text.p: Irish national airline Aer Lingus said on Tuesday that it had concluded negotiations for a strategic alliance between its engine overhaul subsidiary, Airmotive Ireland, and Lufthansa Technik, a subsidiary of Deutsche Lufthansa AG.
Under the terms of the agreement, Lufthansa Technik will acquire a 60 percent shareholding in the Irish engine overhaul company which employs more than 400 staff.
The new company will be known as Lufthansa Airmotive Ireland, Aer Lingus said in a statement.
The airline did not reveal the consideration involved but said it was very satisfied with the outcome of the negotiations and full value was secured for the 60 percent stake.
Aer Lingus said conclusion of the alliance completed another major element of its restructuring programme.

"It was one of our prime objectives to secure Airmotive's future and to strengthen its employment potential by attracting a quality partner with a strong international presence," chief executive Gary McGann said.
The Irish government welcomed the announcement, noting that Airmotive was a major employer in the Dublin area.

"The alliance with Lufthansa -- who have not been one of its customers -- will assure the company's future as well as offering the prospect of additional job opportunities and development of the engine overhaul business in southwest Dublin," Pat Rabbitte, minister for science and technology said.
Airmotive, which was established in 1980, specialises in the overhaul of Pratt and Whitney JT8D, JT9D and CFM56 engines.
